description: A documented, acknowledged code of conduct sets the tone for integrity and ethical behaviour across the organization.
implementation_guidance: Publish a code of conduct covering ethics, acceptable use and confidentiality, and require every employee and contractor to sign it at hire and annually.
name: Code of conduct and ethics policy

description: Consistent consequences for policy violations hold people accountable and deter misconduct.
implementation_guidance: Define a disciplinary process in policy, apply it when violations occur, and retain sanction records.
name: Documented disciplinary process

description: Clear reporting lines and authorities ensure everyone knows who owns security responsibilities.
implementation_guidance: Maintain a current org chart and role descriptions that include security duties, reviewed at least annually.
name: Organizational structure and reporting lines

description: A named owner is accountable for the security program and its outcomes.
implementation_guidance: Formally designate a CISO or security lead in policy or by board resolution, with defined authority and escalation paths.
name: Designated security officer

description: Independent oversight of the security program is a core governance expectation.
implementation_guidance: Put security posture, incidents and risk on the board or oversight-body agenda at least annually and document the meetings.
name: Board / executive security oversight

description: Regular leadership review ensures deficiencies are seen and acted on by the people who can resource fixes.
implementation_guidance: Hold a recurring (quarterly recommended) management review of control health, findings and remediation, with minutes.
name: Periodic management review of security

description: Every control needs an accountable owner or it will not be operated reliably.
implementation_guidance: Map each control to a named owner and keep the mapping current as people change roles.
name: Assigned control ownership (RACI)

description: Objectives must be defined clearly enough that risks to them can be identified.
implementation_guidance: Document the system, the commitments made to customers, and the requirements that follow, and anchor the risk assessment to them.
name: System description and service commitments

description: A documented, recurring risk assessment is the backbone of the program.
implementation_guidance: Perform a formal risk assessment at least annually and on major change, scoring likelihood and impact against defined objectives.
name: Annual risk assessment

description: Risks must be tracked with owners, ratings and a treatment decision to be managed.
implementation_guidance: Maintain a register capturing inherent and residual risk, owner, and treatment (accept/mitigate/transfer/avoid), linked to controls.
name: Risk register with treatment decisions

description: Selected mitigations must be planned and tracked to reduce risk to acceptable levels.
implementation_guidance: For each material risk, record the treatment actions, owner and due dates, and track them to closure.
name: Risk treatment plan

description: SOC 2 explicitly requires fraud, including insider misuse, to be considered.
implementation_guidance: Add a fraud/insider-threat section to the risk assessment and map it to mitigations such as least privilege and logging.
name: Fraud and insider-threat consideration

description: Significant changes can introduce new risks that must be assessed out of cycle.
implementation_guidance: Define triggers (new subprocessor, major architecture change, new data type) that force a documented mini risk review.
name: Change-triggered risk review

description: Controls must demonstrably mitigate identified risks, with no orphan risks.
implementation_guidance: Maintain an explicit mapping of risks to mitigating controls and flag any risk with no control or documented acceptance.
name: Risk-to-control mapping

description: Technology-general controls (access, change, operations) underpin every other control.
implementation_guidance: Ensure the full technology footprint is inventoried and covered by access, change-management and operations controls.
name: IT general controls coverage

description: Written, approved policies deploy controls consistently across the organization.
implementation_guidance: Maintain the standard policy set (InfoSec, access, change, IR, BC/DR, vendor, data, acceptable use, secure development), approved and versioned.
name: Security policy suite

description: Stale policies are a top audit exception; policies must match practice.
implementation_guidance: Review and re-approve every policy at least annually, tracking review dates and version history.
name: Annual policy review

description: Ongoing evaluation proves controls operate throughout the period, not just at a point in time.
implementation_guidance: Run automated checks continuously against connected systems and review failures with owners.
name: Continuous control monitoring

description: Independent testing surfaces weaknesses internal monitoring misses.
implementation_guidance: Commission an external penetration test at least annually and track findings to remediation against SLA.
name: Annual penetration test

description: A periodic internal review catches gaps before the external auditor does.
implementation_guidance: Perform an internal control review or readiness assessment ahead of the audit window and document the results.
name: Internal audit / readiness assessment

description: Identified deficiencies must be routed, tracked and closed, or formally accepted.
implementation_guidance: Track every finding with an owner, severity-based SLA and closure evidence, escalating aging or critical items.
name: Deficiency remediation tracking

description: Knowing your legal, regulatory and contractual commitments is a prerequisite to meeting them.
implementation_guidance: Maintain a register of applicable obligations and map them to the controls that satisfy each.
name: Compliance obligations register

description: Staff can only follow policies they can find and have acknowledged.
implementation_guidance: Publish policies where all staff can access them and track acknowledgments at hire and on change.
name: Internal policy portal

description: People need a known, easy way to report suspected security issues.
implementation_guidance: Operate a dedicated channel (e.g. a security Slack channel or security@ alias) and communicate it to all staff.
name: Security incident reporting channel

description: A confidential reporting path supports the integrity and accountability criteria.
implementation_guidance: Provide an anonymous reporting mechanism and document how reports are handled.
name: Whistleblower / ethics reporting mechanism

description: Customers must be told your security, availability and privacy commitments.
implementation_guidance: Publish terms of service, SLA, a security/trust page and privacy policy, kept current with actual practice.
name: External security commitments

description: Contractual breach-notification promises must be defined and honoured.
implementation_guidance: Document breach-notification timeframes to customers and ensure the incident process triggers them.
name: Customer breach-notification commitment

description: Background screening reduces the risk of granting access to unsuitable individuals.
implementation_guidance: Run background checks (where legally permitted) before granting production access, and retain completion records.
name: Pre-hire background checks

description: Trained staff are the first line of defence; training gaps are a frequent exception.
implementation_guidance: Deliver security-awareness training at onboarding and at least annually, tracking 100% completion.
name: Security awareness training

description: Competence starts with defining the qualifications and duties a role requires.
implementation_guidance: Maintain role descriptions that state required qualifications and security responsibilities.
name: Job descriptions with security responsibilities

description: A consistent onboarding process ensures access, training and acknowledgments happen every time.
implementation_guidance: Use a per-hire checklist covering access request/approval, policy acknowledgment and training assignment.
name: Onboarding checklist

description: A single ex-employee with live access is a severe finding; offboarding must be reliable and timely.
implementation_guidance: Trigger deprovisioning on termination across all systems within a defined SLA and verify it completed.
name: Offboarding and deprovisioning

description: Contractual confidentiality obligations protect customer and company information.
implementation_guidance: Require signed confidentiality and IP agreements from all employees and contractors.
name: Confidentiality / IP agreements

description: Ongoing performance management sustains a competent workforce.
implementation_guidance: Run a documented performance-review process for staff.
name: Performance management

description: Contractors carry the same access risk as employees and are a common offboarding gap.
implementation_guidance: Track contractors with end dates, apply the same onboarding/offboarding, and review their access.
name: Contractor lifecycle management

description: Centralizing authentication improves control over access and makes revocation reliable.
implementation_guidance: Enable SSO across all critical systems that support it and route access through the identity provider.
name: Enforce single sign-on

description: MFA is the single highest-value control against account compromise.
implementation_guidance: Require MFA for all users, and phishing-resistant MFA for administrators, with no broad exclusions.
name: Enforce multi-factor authentication

description: Strong authentication requirements reduce credential-based attacks.
implementation_guidance: Enforce a password policy (length, complexity, breach checks) in the identity provider.
name: Password policy

description: Shared and stored secrets must be encrypted and shared safely, not over chat.
implementation_guidance: Provide a company password manager and require its use for shared credentials.
name: Company password manager

description: Access should be granted by role and limited to what the job requires.
implementation_guidance: Define roles/groups rather than ad-hoc grants and provision access based on least privilege.
name: Role-based access and least privilege

description: Every account should have an authorization trail before credentials are issued.
implementation_guidance: Require documented approval for access requests, especially privileged access, via ticket or workflow.
name: Access provisioning approval

description: Access must be removed promptly when no longer authorized.
implementation_guidance: Remove access on role change or termination within a defined SLA and reconcile active accounts to active staff.
name: Timely access removal

description: Recertifying access catches privilege creep and missed removals.
implementation_guidance: Run access-review campaigns (quarterly for critical systems) where owners certify each user, and verify revocations execute.
name: Periodic user access reviews

description: Admin and root access carry the highest risk and need tighter control.
implementation_guidance: Inventory privileged accounts, require approval for admin grants, and review them at higher frequency.
name: Privileged access management

description: Separating conflicting duties reduces fraud and error risk.
implementation_guidance: Separate sensitive duties where feasible (e.g. deployer is not sole approver) or document compensating controls.
name: Segregation of duties

description: Non-human identities are often over-privileged and unreviewed.
implementation_guidance: Inventory service accounts and API keys, scope them least-privilege, and rotate/review them.
name: Service and machine account governance

description: Idle and long-lived sessions widen the window for hijacking.
implementation_guidance: Configure session timeouts and re-authentication for sensitive systems.
name: Session timeout and management

description: Encrypting stored data protects it if underlying media is exposed.
implementation_guidance: Enable encryption at rest on every data store using cloud-native KMS and verify no store is unencrypted.
name: Encryption at rest

description: Data in motion must be protected from interception.
implementation_guidance: Enforce TLS 1.2+ on all external endpoints, HTTPS-only (HSTS), and deny non-TLS access to storage.
name: Encryption in transit (TLS)

description: Keys must be protected and rotated for encryption to be meaningful.
implementation_guidance: Manage keys in a KMS with access controls and rotation, separate from the data they protect.
name: Encryption key management

description: Secrets in code are a leading breach cause.
implementation_guidance: Store secrets in a vault or secrets manager, never in source, and rotate on exposure.
name: Secrets management

description: Segmentation limits blast radius and keeps data stores off the public network.
implementation_guidance: Place databases in private subnets, default-deny security groups, and separate trust zones.
name: Network segmentation

description: Only explicitly required inbound traffic should be allowed.
implementation_guidance: Configure firewalls/security groups to deny by default and review for 0.0.0.0/0 on sensitive ports.
name: Default-deny firewall rules

description: Internet-exposed SSH/RDP is a common, high-severity finding.
implementation_guidance: Block SSH/RDP from the internet and require access via VPN, zero-trust or a bastion/SSM.
name: No management ports exposed to the internet

description: Public endpoints need protection against web attacks and volumetric floods.
implementation_guidance: Front public services with a WAF and DDoS protection (e.g. Cloudflare, AWS WAF/Shield).
name: WAF and DDoS protection

description: Internal admin access should not rely on network location alone.
implementation_guidance: Require a VPN or zero-trust mesh with MFA for administrative access to infrastructure.
name: VPN / zero-trust remote access

description: Cloud workloads need detection for malicious activity and misconfiguration.
implementation_guidance: Enable a threat-detection service (e.g. GuardDuty) and route findings to the on-call process.
name: Infrastructure threat detection

description: Systems configured to a hardened baseline resist common attacks.
implementation_guidance: Apply CIS or equivalent hardening baselines to infrastructure and check for drift on a schedule.
name: Hardening baselines (CIS)

description: Encrypted laptops make loss or disposal safe.
implementation_guidance: Enforce full-disk encryption on all endpoints and report compliance from MDM.
name: Endpoint full-disk encryption

description: Endpoints are a primary malware entry point.
implementation_guidance: Deploy EDR/anti-malware on all endpoints with enforced auto-update and monitor agent health.
name: Endpoint EDR / anti-malware

description: Managed devices can enforce encryption, patching and wipe.
implementation_guidance: Enroll all endpoints in MDM and reconcile enrolled devices against the employee roster.
name: Device management (MDM) enrollment

description: Unpatched systems are exploited faster than they are noticed.
implementation_guidance: Define OS and software patch SLAs and enforce timely updates via MDM/automation.
name: Patch management

description: Devices leaving the company must not carry recoverable data.
implementation_guidance: Issue and confirm a remote wipe for departing employees and lost devices, retaining the confirmation.
name: Remote wipe on offboarding / loss

description: Unattended, unlocked devices expose data and sessions.
implementation_guidance: Enforce automatic screen lock with a short idle timeout via MDM.
name: Screen lock policy

description: You cannot protect confidential data consistently until it is identified and classified.
implementation_guidance: Adopt a classification scheme (public/internal/confidential/restricted) with handling rules per level.
name: Data classification policy

description: Knowing where confidential and personal data lives is prerequisite to protecting it.
implementation_guidance: Maintain a data map of stores and vendors holding confidential/personal data and the protections applied.
name: Data inventory and data map

description: Data should not be kept longer than needed for its purpose.
implementation_guidance: Define retention periods per data type and enforce them technically (lifecycle rules, TTL jobs).
name: Data retention schedule

description: Data must be irrecoverable once its retention ends or on a valid erasure request.
implementation_guidance: Delete data across primary stores, indexes, caches, analytics and vendors, and age it out of backups.
name: Secure data disposal

description: Copying production data into dev/staging is a frequent confidentiality exception.
implementation_guidance: Populate lower environments with masked or synthetic data and verify prod data does not leak.
name: No production data in lower environments

description: Data subjects must be told what personal information is collected and why.
implementation_guidance: Publish and version a privacy notice covering collection, use, sharing, retention and rights, kept truthful to actual flows.
name: Privacy notice

description: Where consent is required it must be captured, recorded and revocable, including explicit consent for sensitive data.
implementation_guidance: Capture granular consent where required, store consent records, and honour opt-outs downstream.
name: Consent and choice management

description: Collecting only what is needed reduces privacy risk and exposure.
implementation_guidance: Map collection points to stated purposes, avoid unneeded fields, and keep PI out of logs and error trackers.
name: Data minimization

description: Personal data must only be used for the purposes disclosed.
implementation_guidance: Restrict PI access to purpose-based roles, govern secondary uses, and document the AI/training stance.
name: Limit personal-information use to purpose

description: Subjects have a right to access their data and an accounting of disclosures.
implementation_guidance: Operate a DSAR process with identity verification, cross-system compilation and an SLA, logging every request.
name: Data-subject access request process

description: Subjects can require inaccurate data to be corrected and propagated.
implementation_guidance: Provide a correction path, propagate changes to processors, and reconcile PI across systems for quality.
name: Personal-information correction

description: Personal data may only be disclosed as disclosed and consented, with a record kept.
implementation_guidance: Gate third-party data flows through the vendor process and maintain a disclosure register.
name: Authorized-disclosure governance

description: Detected breaches and near-misses must be recorded with PI impact.
implementation_guidance: Record privacy incidents in the incident register with data affected, subject count and root cause.
name: Unauthorized-disclosure recordkeeping

description: Your privacy commitments must flow down to processors of personal data.
implementation_guidance: Execute DPAs with every PI-touching vendor and track DPA coverage as a completeness metric.
name: Data processing agreements with vendors

description: Vendors must commit to notifying you of incidents so you can meet your obligations.
implementation_guidance: Ensure DPAs contain breach-notification clauses with timeframes and record them per vendor.
name: Vendor breach-notification terms

description: Regulators and affected parties must be notified as law and contract require.
implementation_guidance: Build notification criteria, jurisdiction matrices and templates into the incident-response plan.
name: Breach notification process

description: A tracked process for privacy inquiries and complaints is a Privacy-category requirement.
implementation_guidance: Publish a privacy contact, route it into a tracked queue with SLAs, and review privacy compliance periodically.
name: Privacy inquiry and complaint handling

description: Reviewed changes prevent unauthorized or defective code reaching production.
implementation_guidance: Enforce branch protection: PR required, at least one approval, no self-merge, passing status checks.
name: Peer code review (branch protection)

description: Automated tests gate defects and validate processing logic before release.
implementation_guidance: Run automated tests as merge gates and require them to pass before deploy.
name: Automated testing in CI

description: Environment separation prevents untested change and data mixing.
implementation_guidance: Maintain distinct dev, staging and production environments with controlled promotion.
name: Separate dev/staging/production

description: Changes must be authorized, tested and approved before implementation.
implementation_guidance: Require documented authorization and approval for production changes, including database and config changes.
name: Change authorization and approval

description: Hotfixes still need control, applied retroactively where necessary.
implementation_guidance: Define an emergency-change path that requires retroactive review and approval.
name: Emergency change procedure

description: A documented SDLC sets expectations for how software is built and changed.
implementation_guidance: Maintain a secure development policy covering review, testing, environments and deployment.
name: Secure SDLC policy

description: Vulnerable dependencies are a primary supply-chain risk.
implementation_guidance: Enable dependency and container image scanning on all repos and triage alerts to SLA.
name: Dependency and image scanning

description: Committed secrets are routinely harvested by attackers.
implementation_guidance: Enable secret scanning and pre-commit hooks, and rotate any exposed secret immediately.
name: Secret scanning

description: Bad input must be caught at the door to keep processing complete and accurate.
implementation_guidance: Validate inputs at ingestion (schema, type, range, duplicates) and route rejects to a monitored queue.
name: Input validation controls

description: Correct processing can only be tested against a defined specification.
implementation_guidance: Document data definitions, calculation logic and processing SLAs, versioned with the system.
name: Processing specifications

description: Reconciling outputs to inputs proves processing completeness and accuracy.
implementation_guidance: Monitor job execution and reconcile record counts/totals, alerting and investigating breaks.
name: Processing reconciliation and monitoring

description: In-process data must be stored durably and completely.
implementation_guidance: Use durable, versioned storage for pipeline stages with integrity checks and retention aligned to spec.
name: Pipeline storage integrity

description: Reliable logs are the raw material for detection and investigation.
implementation_guidance: Centralize security-relevant logs (audit, auth, application) with retention of at least one year.
name: Centralized logging and retention

description: You cannot secure or monitor what you have not inventoried.
implementation_guidance: Maintain a current inventory of systems and assets, ideally collected automatically from cloud APIs.
name: Asset and system inventory

description: Detection is only useful if anomalies raise alerts someone sees.
implementation_guidance: Alert on security-relevant signals (root use, IAM changes, threat findings) and route to a monitored channel.
name: Security anomaly alerting

description: Alerts need a responder at all hours.
implementation_guidance: Operate an on-call rotation that receives and acknowledges security and availability alerts.
name: On-call rotation

description: New vulnerabilities must be found and remediated on a defined cadence.
implementation_guidance: Scan infrastructure and dependencies regularly and remediate by severity-based SLA, tracking to closure.
name: Vulnerability management program

description: Config changes can silently introduce vulnerabilities.
implementation_guidance: Continuously monitor cloud configuration for drift from a secure baseline and alert on regressions.
name: Configuration-change detection

description: Events must be evaluated to decide whether they are incidents.
implementation_guidance: Define severity classification and keep a triage record for security events, including benign ones.
name: Security event evaluation

description: A defined program contains and remediates incidents predictably.
implementation_guidance: Maintain an IR plan with roles, severities, containment/eradication/recovery and communication steps.
name: Incident response plan

description: Lessons must translate into changes so incidents do not recur.
implementation_guidance: Run postmortems for incidents and track corrective action items to closure.
name: Incident postmortems with actions

description: In a no-incident year, a tabletop is the operating evidence the program works.
implementation_guidance: Run at least an annual tabletop exercise with participants and captured findings.
name: Incident tabletop exercise

description: Recovery from incidents must be defined and executed, not improvised.
implementation_guidance: Include restore/rebuild/credential-rotation procedures in the IR plan and document recovery in incidents.
name: Incident recovery procedures

description: Disruptions must be planned for with defined recovery objectives.
implementation_guidance: Maintain a BC/DR plan with RTO/RPO targets, key dependencies and workarounds, reviewed annually.
name: Business continuity / disaster recovery plan

description: Availability commitments require capacity to be monitored ahead of demand.
implementation_guidance: Monitor utilization with thresholds below failure points and use autoscaling where possible.
name: Capacity management

description: Recoverable backups are the foundation of availability and resilience.
implementation_guidance: Enable automated encrypted backups on every data store with retention aligned to RPO and alert on failures.
name: Automated, monitored backups

description: A backup that has never been restored is only a hypothesis.
implementation_guidance: Test recovery at least annually by restoring a backup and validating data against RTO/RPO.
name: Backup restore testing

description: You must know who your vendors are and what data they touch.
implementation_guidance: Maintain a vendor register with owner, criticality and data-access classification, kept complete.
name: Vendor inventory

description: Vendor risk must be assessed on onboarding and periodically.
implementation_guidance: Review vendor security (SOC 2 report, questionnaire) scaled to risk and re-review critical vendors annually.
name: Vendor security due diligence

description: New SaaS adopted informally creates unmanaged vendor and data risk.
implementation_guidance: Detect new SSO apps and OAuth grants and feed them into the vendor onboarding workflow.
name: Shadow-IT detection

description: Subprocessors receiving customer/personal data must be tracked and (often) published.
implementation_guidance: Maintain a subprocessor list and reconcile it against vendors actually receiving data.
name: Subprocessor management

description: Cloud data-center physical security is inherited and must be reviewed, not assumed.
implementation_guidance: Obtain and review the cloud provider's SOC 2 report annually and disclose the carve-out in the system description.
name: Cloud physical security (subservice review)

description: In-scope offices and server areas need access restriction.
implementation_guidance: Where offices are in scope, use badge access, visitor logs and revoke badges on offboarding.
name: Office physical access controls
